requirement_text.REQ-421:
Build-order M2, MOB-2 in docs/mobile/requirements.md. The gate for the whole tier: after this, a build can log into a tenant. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (authentication flow, token handling).
SEQUENCE: 1. Tenant identity from manual slug entry or a deep link (https://<slug>.<platform-host>/..., Android intent filter for https with host *.<platform-host>, where <platform-host> is supplied at build time from the same build configuration as LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL -- e.g. a --dart-define plus a Gradle manifestPlaceholder -- never a tenant slug; iOS universal-link entitlement written but DEFERRED -- no iOS build on this host). Verified App Link status (android:autoVerify) needs /.well-known/assetlinks.json served by the platform host, which no requirement provides: declare the filter without relying on verification and record verification as DEFERRED with that reason. The slug is the only tenant input; nothing tenant specific is compiled in (REQ-419's guard stays green). 2. GET {LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL}/api/mobile/tenant-config?slug=<slug> with NO Authorization header. Consume realm_url, client_id (added by REQ-418), locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind. The endpoint never errors on an unknown slug: by its anti-enumeration never-error rule it returns platform defaults, including realm_url for the default realm "bpm-default" (@default_realm, lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex:151,199). The app therefore CANNOT detect an unknown slug before login, and must not try to (that would be the enumeration oracle the endpoint refuses to be). "Tenant not found" is detected AFTER login instead: the FIRST entry of GET /api/v1/me/memberships is always the tenant the token itself serves (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex moduledoc, "Response shape": the handler prepends the caller's own current tenant); every later entry is a tenant the subject could switch into by re-authenticating, and the backend scopes every request to the token's tenant, not to the slug the user typed. So: if the first entry's tenant_slug does not equal the entered slug, show tenant-not-found and delete the just-stored tokens -- even when a later entry matches (matching any entry would let the app label tenant A's data as tenant B's; v1 does not perform the re-authentication a switch needs). CANDIDATE users get 403 from /me/memberships by design (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex, "MembershipsRead -- CANDIDATE deliberately excluded"); on that 403 skip the membership check and rely on /me/modules. Document this rule in code comments. 3. flutter_appauth authorizeAndExchangeCode with issuer = realm_url, clientId = client_id from step 2 (never a compiled constant), redirectUrl com.bizdala.letflow:/oauth2redirect, PKCE S256 (flutter_appauth default). Android: Custom Tabs via the appAuthRedirectScheme manifest placeholder; no webview anywhere (REQ-419's dependency guard forbids webview packages). 4. Tokens persisted ONLY through one class in lib/auth/ backed by flutter_secure_storage, keyed by tenant (realm_url) so tenant A's tokens are never presented to tenant B. REQ-422 hardens and guards this; REQ-421 must not introduce any other storage path for tokens. 5. Before any tenant content: GET /api/v1/me/memberships and GET /api/v1/me/modules (lib/letflow/routers/me.ex:74, :78) and build the route table from installed_modules (architecture.md §6 -- a module not installed has no route at all). 6. Four dedicated error screens: tenant-not-found, network-unavailable, OIDC-failure, secure-storage-unavailable. 7. Create lib/api/api_client.dart as the ONLY place a Dio instance is constructed (bearer attach only; refresh/retry/typed errors are REQ-425's). All HTTP in this and later requirements goes through it. 8. docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2's first acceptance bullet and docs/mobile/architecture.md §3 row 1 list the five-key tenant-config shape; append a dated note to each that REQ-418 added client_id as a sixth key and that the app consumes it (keep the original text).
LIVE LOGIN caveat: completing a real Keycloak login requires typing credentials into a Custom Tab, which `flutter test` cannot drive. Acceptance is therefore split: the full sequence is proven by widget /unit tests with a fake AppAuth adapter and a fake HTTP layer; a live emulator run proves the app reaches Keycloak's login page for two different slugs; the interactive credential entry is DEFERRED to UAT-RUNNER with that reason recorded.

result.summary:
Ran `git diff main...HEAD --stat` (39 files, all under apps/mobile/, docs/mobile/*.md dated-note additions, docs/requirements.yaml status flip, and one new lib/letflow/design/req421-mobile-tenant-bootstrap.md design doc; no lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ Elixir code touched) and read the substantive diffs directly (apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth.dart, apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart, apps/mobile/lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart, apps/mobile/lib/app.dart, docs/mobile/architecture.md, docs/mobile/requirements.md, docs/requirements.yaml, apps/mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts, apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, apps/mobile/ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements, apps/mobile/test/guards/*).

1. Idiomatic vs. crutch (Dart-appropriate sense: proper Riverpod provider usage, no ad-hoc global mutable state substituting for it) -- PASS. State is wired through real Riverpod providers (flutterSecureStorageProvider -> tenantTokenStoreProvider -> apiClientProvider, activeRealmHolderProvider, bootstrapControllerProvider) declared once in navigation_bootstrap.dart and consumed via ref.watch in both TenantSlugEntryScreen and app.dart's LetflowApp/ConsumerWidget -- no second wiring path, no static/global mutable singleton standing in for a provider. BootstrapController is a plain ChangeNotifier driving GoRouter's refreshListenable/redirect, which is the standard go_router+Riverpod idiom, not a hand-rolled state machine impersonating a real one. ActiveRealmHolder is a small mutable holder by design (documented as intentionally mutable, not a build-time constant, so a second bootstrap can overwrite it) -- this is a narrow, justified exception, not a general crutch pattern, and it is itself threaded through the provider graph rather than reached for as a bare global.

2. Supervision-equivalent / isolation integrity (single-Dio-construction and single-token-store invariants the design fixed) -- PASS. ApiClient.create is the sole production Dio(...) construction site (api_client.dart's own moduledoc states the grep invariant; confirmed by reading the file -- ApiClient.forTesting takes a caller-built Dio for tests, it does not construct a second one inside lib/). TenantTokenStore in auth.dart is the sole class touching flutter_secure_storage (moduledoc states this; no other file in the diff calls FlutterSecureStorage directly). Token-store keying is by realmUrl, not the entered slug (TenantTokenStore._keyFor(realmUrl)), consistent with tenant-isolation intent. No competing storage or HTTP-construction path was introduced anywhere in the diff.

3. Type-safety gaps -- none worth a new docs/issues/ filing beyond what SECURITY-REVIEWER already covered. BootstrapPhase/BootstrapFailureReason are enums and BootstrapResult is a sealed-style union (BootstrapSuccess/BootstrapFailure) exhaustively switched over in buildErrorScreen and BootstrapController.beginBootstrap -- this is the struct/enum-shaped design the reviewer.md question asks for, not a stringly-typed or map-shaped result. TenantConfig.fromJson is total and throws FormatException on any missing/malformed key rather than returning a partially-populated object, which forecloses an invalid-tenant-config runtime class before it reaches call sites. No new invalid-state class was found that a type change would make unrepresentable; nothing filed.

4. Scope creep -- none found. Every changed file sits inside REQ-421's owned_modules (apps/mobile/, docs/mobile/requirements.md, docs/mobile/architecture.md) plus the expected docs/requirements.yaml status flip and status-history volume append. The two docs/mobile/*.md edits are dated notes appending REQ-418's client_id key (keeping original text, as REQ-421's own task said to) -- not a rewrite of prior content. No new abstraction layer, behaviour, or generic plumbing appears ahead of need: HttpGateway is a narrow two-method interface sized exactly to this requirement's callers (get/getUnauthenticated), not a general HTTP-client abstraction; buildRouteTable's real output is the empty set since REQ-421 ships zero feature modules, and the code says so in comments rather than pretending otherwise. flutter_secure_storage_platform_interface was added as a dev_dependency only, for test fakes -- consistent with 0012's stack (flutter_secure_storage itself, already on record) and does not add a new production dependency. The Android/iOS deep-link and universal-link wiring matches REQ-421's own requirement text exactly (autoVerify=false with DEFERRED reasoning recorded in-line, iOS entitlement written but DEFERRED, platform-host sourced from build config not a compiled tenant slug) -- no verification infrastructure was speculatively built ahead of a requirement that explicitly said not to.

docs/anti-patterns.md check: grepped for mobile/Flutter/Dart/Riverpod/Dio-relevant entries; none apply to this diff's content (the two hits found are about REVIEWER's own gate and an unrelated multipart-test idiom).

Decision-record consistency (0012-mobile-tier-stack.md): stack usage matches exactly -- Riverpod, Dio, flutter_appauth (OIDC Auth-Code+PKCE, Custom Tabs, no webview -- reconfirmed by the unchanged-logic reformatting of forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart still passing over this diff's dependency set), flutter_secure_storage. No re-decision of 0012 attempted or implied anywhere in the diff.

The two MOBILE-DEV-recorded MINOR notes, assessed as reasonable corrections rather than silent deviations needing CODE-DESIGNER rework:
(a) flutter_appauth 12.1.0 throwing FlutterAppAuthUserCancelledException instead of the design's assumed null-return: RealAppAuthAdapter absorbs exactly that one exception type and returns null, preserving the AppAuthAdapter interface's documented null-on-cancel contract unchanged for every caller (authenticateWithTenant, runTenantBootstrap, BootstrapController). This is a pinned-dependency-version adaptation at the narrowest possible seam -- it does not change the design's contract, only which mechanism satisfies it, and is thoroughly commented in place. No design ambiguity was resolved unilaterally in a way that changes observable behavior; this did not need to go back to CODE-DESIGNER.
(b) Active-realm-pointer-set-immediately-after-store ordering: setting activeRealm.currentRealmUrl right after token store succeeds (rather than after the memberships/modules checks) is required for those same calls' bearer-attach interceptor to find a token at all, and every subsequent failure branch (membership mismatch, non-200/403 status, exception, modules failure) explicitly resets the pointer to null before returning a BootstrapFailure -- verified by reading all five failure branches. This is an implementation-level sequencing detail the design under-specified, resolved the only way that makes the described interceptor behavior possible, not a scope or security deviation. Also independently confirmed safe by SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c pass (same ordering, checked against INV-4/INV-6). No rework needed.

No BLOCKER or MINOR idiom/scope findings. No docs/issues/ filing needed (no unrepresentable-invalid-state gap found beyond what's already type-safe).
